title: Effort and technical gotchas
objective: Identify four effort risks for a cross-system agent that updates a CRM record.
clearance: Rewritten draft; pending SME and partner clearance

blocks.x: Effort is where optimistic use cases fail. A simple-sounding request can depend on several systems, complex permissions, or actions that require security review. Surface these risks in discovery, not after a demo.
Glean's partner enablement lists technical gotchas to surface in discovery:

blocks.caption: Technical gotchas
head: Area
What to watch for
Question to ask
rows: Data and connectors
The source of truth is unclear; no native connector; immature or rate-limited APIs; on-premises systems
"Where is the canonical record, and which system wins on conflicts?"
Data footprint
A small-sounding use case needs legacy systems, archives, or large files
"How much history does this need?"
Permissions and identity
Row- or field-level permissions; multiple directories; shared mailboxes; exceptions
"Who can see what, and are there exceptions?"
Structured expectations
Expecting exact joins and aggregations from a chat prompt when the use case needs deterministic SQL or BI
"Is this a lookup or a calculation?"
Freshness
Needing real-time results for data indexed periodically
"How current must the answer be?"
Actions and write-backs
Assuming the agent can update any system; multi-step transactions; security review of write actions
"What exactly would be written, by whom, with what audit?"
Data quality and taxonomy
Inconsistent labels; knowledge only in private chats or local drives
"Where does the real answer live today?"

blocks.x: Validate feasibility with the people who own the systems. Don't infer it from a use case description. Also consider change management. A technically easy use case still takes effort if it changes how a team works.

blocks.label: Boundary
blocks.x: Don't claim that generic retrieval will perform deterministic joins, or that an agent can write to any system. Verify current capabilities with the Glean account team, and get owner commitments before rating a use case as easy.
Effort hides in the data. Ask system owners about these areas before you rank a use case as low effort.

blocks.title: Where effort hides
blocks.alt: Six cards naming common sources of hidden effort: unclear sources of truth and connectors, permissions and identity, structured data expectations, data freshness, actions and write-backs, and data quality.

items.label: Connectors
items.detail: Is there a clear source of truth and a connector?

items.label: Permissions
items.detail: Row- or field-level rules; multiple identities

items.label: Write-backs
items.detail: Which systems may the agent update?

practice.x: A use case calls for an agent that reads five systems and updates a CRM record after each customer call. Identify at least four effort risks.

items: **Connector availability** for all five systems, and whether each source is canonical.
**Identity and permissions:** whether users see only the records they're entitled to.
**Data consistency** across systems, such as conflicting account names or fields.
**An approved write-action model:** what is written, and the audit trail, idempotency, and handling of partial failures.
**Security review** of write actions into the CRM.

worked.x: Mark each as unresolved and assign a validation owner before rating effort.
